A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bilevel fine-tuning and concept-suppression framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on distillation, pruning, artist-style removal, NSFW suppression, and adversarial robustness.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments with AdvUnlearn and an alternative unlearning/pruning/distillation order.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an AdvUnlearn-based instantiation of the framework, whereas v1 evaluates its bilevel method with ESD. This changes the unlearning component used in that variant; the core formulation and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Table 3 adds evaluation using adversarial NSFW prompts attributed to Zhang et al. [4]. Existing COCO, artist-erasure, I2P, MMA, and Ring-a-Bell coverage remains. Continual unlearning is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds Distilled Model + AdvUnlearn and an ESD-first unlearn-prune-distill comparator in Appendix C.2. Existing comparisons against ESD, UCE, and ConceptPrune are retained.

E3.justification: The new appendix comparison reports attack success rate (ASR), while original training budgets and evaluation settings are retained. v2 also calls the CP metric's reference model 'unpruned,' conflicting with its unchanged distilled-model reference explanation and Table 1; an actual experimental reference change cannot be established.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2.1 adds a pipeline-order control testing unlearning before pruning and distillation. Additional adversarial evaluation examines whether the framework's benefits extend to AdvUnlearn. Existing pruning/distillation analyses and robustness tests remain.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported experiments. The new table continues reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, with v1 Tables 2 and 3 combined into v2 Table 2. New Table 3 reports ASR/FID of 32.4/26.91 for bilevel AdvUnlearn versus 36.6/36.17 for its two-stage counterpart, alongside other added results. Figure 8 adds generated samples.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and penalty/minimax derivations in Sections 3-4 and Appendix B remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: joint fine-tuning and unlearning, compatibility with different pruning/unlearning methods, and improved trade-offs over sequential pipelines. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 discusses potential interference during continual unlearning and identifies it as future work. Appendix C.2 explains poorer unlearn-first generation quality as degradation inherited through distillation from an already altered teacher.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository hyperlink in the abstract. Existing hardware, hyperparameter, and sampling details in Appendix C.1 are retained; similarly detailed settings for the added AdvUnlearn experiments are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 newly cites Mixture of Efficient Diffusion Experts, Receler, and AdvUnlearn, with AdvUnlearn also entering the experiments. The broader positioning relative to pruning and concept-unlearning research remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the conclusion, makes localized wording edits, updates author affiliations, and adds Section 5.3 and Appendix C.2. The existing Figure Prompts subsection moves from C.2 to C.3; most prose and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 merges the original adversarial-robustness and COCO-retention tables, adds an appendix results table and Figure 8's sample grid, and adjusts captions and figure sizing. Original figures and prompt tables are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added AdvUnlearn and reversed-order comparisons strengthen support for the framework's modularity and pipeline choice, and the code link improves reproducibility information. These gains are limited by sparse settings for the new experiments, continued absence of uncertainty estimates, and newly inconsistent CP-reference wording.
